facts.text: Manhattan Valley Development Corporation, founded in 1968, became a model for community‑based planning and affordable housing projects that guided the neighborhood’s recovery.
The area was originally home to working‑class families and immigrants, and it still maintains its multicultural roots today.
Manhattan Valley sits within Manhattan, a borough that was once part of Lenapehoking territory inhabited by the Munsee, Lenape, and Wappinger tribes.
According to a Munsee tradition, the island was named for a grove of hickory trees ideal for bowmaking.
The 1965 landmark law enacted after Penn Station’s demolition helped preserve historic sites across Manhattan, setting a precedent for the borough’s preservation efforts.
